text: Wall Street just had a brutal day. The Dow lost more than eleven hundred points.
The S&P 500 fell two percent, its sixth straight loss. And the tech-heavy Nasdaq, home of the AI giants, fell even more.
Domino one: AI leadership. Nvidia, the face of the boom, lost its CEO, and a short seller hit AMD.
Domino two: the AI IPO test. Anthropic opened up thirty-four percent, then gave back half. It could not revive the AI trade.
Domino three: rates. Markets expect another Fed hike, and higher rates hit the priciest growth stocks first.
Now, perspective. Since 1980, the S&P 500 has dropped about fourteen percent at some point in an average year. And still finished higher in roughly three out of four years.
Eight percent off the top hurts. It is not unusual.
Your call: is this the AI bubble popping, or just a dip? Comment BUBBLE or DIP.
